analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers Newton three laws of motion with inertia, force as change in momentum, F equals m times a for constant mass, and action reaction with airplane flight examples

overview.headline: Newton laws link inertia force and motion for flight

keyPoints.point: Objects that remain at rest or keep constant motion unless unbalanced force acts show inertia
keyPoints.quote: unless acted on by an unbalanced force

keyPoints.point: Acceleration of an object depends on its mass and the amount of applied force
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyPoints.point: Second object exerts equal opposite force when first object exerts force during interaction
keyPoints.quote: Whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.

keyPoints.point: Relation F equals m times a is only good for objects that have constant mass
keyPoints.quote: Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.

keyTerms.gloss: tendency to resist changes in motion when forces cancel
keyTerms.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: changes in momentum defined by mass times velocity
keyTerms.quote: Newton’s second law talks about changes in momentum (m V).

keyTerms.gloss: definition of acceleration as change in velocity divided by change in time
keyTerms.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.

keyTerms.gloss: quantity having magnitude and direction like force
keyTerms.quote: Scientists and mathematicians call this a vector quantity.

keyTerms.gloss: constant mass for which force equals mass times acceleration remains valid
keyTerms.quote: Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.
